I’ll search offsets within one lattice period for a placement that preserves the maximum number of complete cells while maximizing the minimum edge margin.

The absolute maximum count (85) still requires point contact. I’ll select the largest count with at least 0.25 mm clearance, sufficient to remove the topological singularity without inventing a large frame.
A half-row vertical shift gives 72 complete passages and a 2.195 mm minimum frame margin, avoiding all tangencies. I’ll rebuild the final fluid solid with that offset and remeasure it.

The final coarse CAD volume is one connected solid. I’ll now tessellate and render it with an oblique cutaway so the upstream/downstream duct and hexagonal core passages are visible rather than hidden by the outer duct walls.

The cutaway confirms the intended topology: open plenums connected only through the hexagonal passages. The conformal surface is closed and clean, so I’ll immediately create a coarse snappyHexMesh setup: a 4 mm background grid, one refinement level to about 2 mm on all named surfaces, and an interior seed in the upstream plenum.
